exam.subject: General Knowledge
exam.school: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examination (ESSCE) – national
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2023 – General Knowledge (3133)

parts.title: Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: This Examination Paper contains 100 Multiple Choice Questions only. You must answer all of them. Each question carries one point. There is only one best answer for each question; blacken the letter of your choice on the SCANTRON GENERAL PURPOSE ANSWER SHEET with a pencil.

variants.note: Same 100 items and options in a different order (shuffled mostly within blocks of ten). question_map gives 3133 number → 3134 number. Items 16–20 and 36–40 of form 3134 are missing from the scan, so the 3134 numbers of 3133 items 11, 14, 17, 18, 22, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40 could not be confirmed (they are 3134 items 16–20 and 36–40 in some order: 11, 14, 17, 18, 22 → 16–20; 32, 34, 36, 38, 40 → 36–40).

source.prepared_by: National Higher Education and Research Institute, Eritrea – ESSCE 2023, General Knowledge, exam code 3133
source.conversion_notes: Nitro image PDF (page 2 = copyright page; page 23 blank). Text from tesseract OCR, checked line by line against the page images; garbled OCR re-keyed from the images (items 21, 29, 37, 38, 51, 56, 80, 87, 88 and several option lines). Words printed bold and underlined (is not, different, biggest, tallest, fastest, odd, is/are not, highest, missing, longest, oldest, is different) are marked <u>…</u>. Bold phrases that are not underlined (‘Contempt’, ‘I think; therefore, I am’) are quoted. Blanks are shown as ____. Item 51 prints 10⁹ twice (options A and E). No figures. Form 3134 (IGNORED as a source) is the same paper scrambled; see exam.variants.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and every fact was checked against reliable general sources (shabait.com for Eritrean facts; encyclopaedias, UN/WHO/agency sites, sports-results sites and news archives for world facts). General Knowledge has no textbook: textbook_ref = {source:'general', reference, time_sensitive}. Current-affairs items are answered as correct at the time of the exam (the 2023 ESSCE was sat 13–18 March 2023 at ten centres including Sawa – shabait.com, 10 and 24 March 2023); later changes are noted in the explanation and ref note.
exam.textbook_note: No General Knowledge textbook: every textbook_ref is a general-source reference {source:'general', reference, topic, accessed, time_sensitive}.

questions.stem: The most southern tip of Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Ras Dumera (Ras Doumeira) is the cape at the south-eastern end of Eritrea's coast, on the border with Djibouti in the Southern Red Sea region.
Karora and Ras Kassar are at the far north (Sudan border); Alghena is in the north (Northern Red Sea); Dadda'to is in the south-east near Djibouti but inland and north of Ras Dumera. Answer: E.
tips: North end: Karora/Ras Kassar. South end: Ras Dumera (border with Djibouti).

similar_questions.stem: Which place is at the northern end of Eritrea, on the border with Sudan?
explanation_steps: Karora lies on the Sudan border at Eritrea's northern tip. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea: land; Ras Doumeira

questions.stem: The livelihood most common in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: About 70–80% of Eritreans live by traditional subsistence agriculture that combines crop growing with keeping livestock – agro-pastoralism (mixed farming).
Those farms are small family farms, so ‘small scale farming’ (A) is also defensible. Fishing, pure pastoralism and agro-industry support far fewer people. Keyed E; A also accepted.
tips: Eritrea's rural systems: sedentary crop–livestock farming (agro-pastoralism), pastoralism, fishing on the coast.

similar_questions.stem: A family that grows sorghum and also keeps goats and cattle practises
explanation_steps: Crops + livestock together = agro-pastoralism (mixed farming). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: IUCN – Pastoralism in Eritrea (country study); UNDP – Eritrea profile (about 80% depend on subsistence crop and livestock farming)

questions.review_flag: Overlapping options (same issue as GK 2021 item 70): most Eritreans practise mixed crop–livestock farming on small farms. Keyed E (agro-pastoralism), A (small scale farming) also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: In 1961, the liberation movement fired the first bullet in the ____ mountain in the ____ Zoba of Eritrea.
explanation_steps: On 1 September 1961 Hamid Idris Awate and his small band fired the first shots of the armed struggle at Mount Adal in western Eritrea.
Mount Adal is in today's Zoba Gash-Barka. Answer: D.
tips: 1 September = start of the armed struggle (Adal, Awate); 24 May = Independence Day; 20 June = Martyrs' Day.

similar_questions.stem: Who led the fighters who fired the first bullet of Eritrea's armed struggle in 1961?
explanation_steps: Hamid Idris Awate started the armed struggle at Mount Adal on 1 September 1961. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – 1st September: the beginning of the armed struggle

questions.stem: One of the following is <u>different</u> from the others.
explanation_steps: Iron, copper, tin and zinc are metals (chemical elements mined as ores).
Oil (petroleum) is a liquid fossil fuel, a mixture of hydrocarbons – not a metal. Answer: D.
tips: Odd-one-out: find the group that four options share (here: metals).

similar_questions.stem: Find the odd one out.
explanation_steps: Gold, silver, lead and aluminium are metals; coal is a fossil fuel. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – Metals; Petroleum

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is the <u>biggest</u>?
explanation_steps: The blue whale, up to about 30 m long and 150–200 tonnes, is the largest animal that has ever lived.
The African elephant (about 6–7 t) is the largest land animal; the giraffe is the tallest. Answer: C.
tips: Largest animal: blue whale; largest land animal: African elephant; tallest: giraffe.

similar_questions.stem: The tallest living land animal is the
explanation_steps: Giraffes reach about 5.5 m. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following <u>is not</u> a traditional source of energy in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: Most Eritrean households have traditionally cooked with biomass: firewood, charcoal, crop residues and dried animal dung.
Eritrea has no coal mining and coal is not a household fuel there. Answer: D.
tips: Biomass fuels = wood, charcoal, dung, crop residues.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a renewable energy source now promoted in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Solar energy is renewable; Eritrea has built solar plants (e.g. Areza, Maidma). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Energy and Mines / UNDP – household energy in Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of the following bird species can fly?
explanation_steps: Ostrich (Africa), penguin (southern oceans), kiwi (New Zealand) and emu (Australia) are all flightless birds.
So none of the listed birds can fly. Answer: E.
tips: Flightless birds: ostrich, emu, rhea, cassowary, kiwi, penguin.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these birds can fly?
explanation_steps: The eagle is a strong flier; the others are flightless. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> made of rubber?
explanation_steps: Tyres, many balls and the soles of gym shoes are made of (natural or synthetic) rubber.
Plastic bags are made of polyethylene (plastic) and leather jackets of tanned animal hide – neither is rubber. Two options fit, so both are accepted. Keyed B; E also accepted.
tips: Rubber products: tyres, balls, shoe soles, erasers, gloves, hoses.

similar_questions.stem: Natural rubber comes from
explanation_steps: Natural rubber is made from latex of the rubber tree (Hevea). Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: Two correct options: plastic bags (B) and leather jackets (E) are both not made of rubber. Keyed B, E also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following buildings is the world’s <u>tallest</u> building at present?
explanation_steps: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai (UAE), opened in 2010, is 828 m tall – the tallest building in the world at the time of the exam (and still in 2026).
The Eiffel Tower (330 m) is a tower, not a building; the Qutb Minar is a 73 m minaret in Delhi. Answer: C.
tips: Burj Khalifa – Dubai – 828 m.

similar_questions.stem: The Burj Khalifa is in
explanation_steps: It is in Dubai, UAE. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: Tallest building as at March 2023 and still in 2026; Jeddah Tower (Saudi Arabia), planned to exceed 1,000 m, was still under construction.

questions.stem: The vitamin that promotes healthy functioning of the eyes in human beings is
explanation_steps: Vitamin A (retinol) is needed to make rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment of the retina; lack of it causes night blindness.
Vitamin C – gums/scurvy; D – bones/rickets; K – blood clotting. Answer: C.
tips: A = eyes, C = scurvy, D = rickets, K = clotting.

similar_questions.stem: Lack of vitamin D in children causes
explanation_steps: Vitamin D is needed for calcium absorption and bone growth. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Vitamin A deficiency

questions.stem: Insert the letter(s) that can be inserted as a prefix to all of the words given to form new meaningful words. __ROW __EATER __AT
explanation_steps: TH + ROW = THROW, TH + EATER = THEATER, TH + AT = THAT – all real words.
Check others: M gives MAT but not MROW; WH gives WHAT but not WHROW; C gives CROW, CAT but not CEATER; DR gives DRAT but not DREATER. Answer: B.
tips: Test each option on the hardest word first (here ‘EATER’).

similar_questions.stem: Which letter(s) can be put in front of all of these to make new words? __INK __ALL __ILL
explanation_steps: W: WINK, WALL, WILL – all words.
H fails (HINK), T fails (TALL works but TINK does not), SH fails (SHINK), B fails (BINK). Answer: D.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard verbal-reasoning practice (dictionary check: throw, theater, that)

questions.stem: Who among the following players is considered the king of football?
explanation_steps: Pelé (Edson Arantes do Nascimento, Brazil, 1940 – died 29 December 2022) won three World Cups (1958, 1962, 1970) and is universally nicknamed ‘O Rei’ – the King of Football.
Maradona, Ronaldo, Messi and Zidane are great players but the title ‘king of football’ belongs to Pelé. Answer: B.
tips: Pelé – Brazil – ‘The King’ – 3 World Cups.

similar_questions.stem: Pelé played for which national team?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: Pelé died on 29 December 2022, less than three months before the exam.

questions.stem: Lunar eclipse occurs when the

options.A: moon is between the earth and the sun.
options.B: sun is between the earth and the moon.
options.C: earth is between the moon and the sun.
options.D: earth is at the farthest distance from the sun.
options.E: moon is at the farthest distance from the sun.

explanation_steps: In a lunar eclipse the Earth lies directly between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the (full) Moon.
Moon between Earth and Sun (A) is a SOLAR eclipse. Answer: C.
tips: Lunar eclipse: Earth in the middle (full moon). Solar eclipse: Moon in the middle (new moon).

similar_questions.stem: A solar eclipse happens when

options.A: the Earth is between the Sun and Moon
options.B: the Moon is between the Sun and Earth
options.C: the Sun is between Earth and Moon
options.E: the Earth is farthest from the Sun

explanation_steps: The Moon blocks the Sun's light from part of the Earth. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Who was elected African Cyclist of the year 2022?
explanation_steps: Biniam Girmay won Gent–Wevelgem (first African to win a cobbled classic) and a stage of the 2022 Giro d'Italia (first Black African Grand Tour stage winner).
In December 2022 he was voted African Cyclist of the Year for the third year in a row. Answer: D.
tips: Biniam Girmay – Intermarché – Gent–Wevelgem 2022, Giro stage 10 2022; in 2024 he also won the Tour de France green jersey.

similar_questions.stem: In 2024 Biniam Girmay became the first Black African to win which Tour de France jersey?
explanation_steps: He won three stages and the green points jersey in 2024. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Cyclingnews – Biniam Girmay voted African Cyclist of the Year for third time in succession (Dec 2022)
textbook_ref.note: As at March 2023. Girmay later won the 2024 Tour de France green jersey.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries won FIFA World Cup 2022?
explanation_steps: The 2022 World Cup in Qatar was won by Argentina, who beat France on penalties (3–3 after extra time) in the final on 18 December 2022.
Answer: B.
tips: 2014 Germany, 2018 France, 2022 Argentina.

similar_questions.stem: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The next World Cup (2026) is hosted by Canada, Mexico and the USA.

questions.stem: A newly hatched butterfly is called a
explanation_steps: A butterfly has complete metamorphosis: egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult.
What hatches from the egg is the larva, the caterpillar. Answer: C.
tips: Egg – caterpillar – chrysalis – butterfly.

similar_questions.stem: The resting stage between caterpillar and adult butterfly is the
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: A fruit seller sells 40% of her apples and she still has 420 apples left. Originally, she had
explanation_steps: After selling 40% she has 60% left: 0.60 × N = 420.
N = 420 ÷ 0.6 = 700 apples. Answer: D.
tips: Remaining % × original = what is left.

similar_questions.stem: A trader sold 25% of his eggs and has 300 left. How many did he have?

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is the <u>fastest</u>?
explanation_steps: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching about 100–110 km/h in short sprints.
Lions and leopards reach about 60–80 km/h, kangaroos about 70 km/h. Answer: A.
tips: Fastest land animal: cheetah; fastest bird (diving): peregrine falcon.

similar_questions.stem: The fastest animal in a dive is the
explanation_steps: Peregrine falcons exceed 300 km/h when diving. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the easiest way to tell the age of trees?

options.A: To measure the width of the tree
options.B: To count the rings on the trunk
options.C: To count the number of leaves
options.D: To measure the height of the tree
options.E: To count the number of branches

explanation_steps: In seasonal climates a tree adds one growth ring of wood each year, so counting the annual rings on a cut trunk (or a core sample) gives its age (dendrochronology).
Answer: B.
tips: One ring ≈ one year.

similar_questions.stem: The study of tree rings to date events is called
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: If Semira’s job is to recruit, develop and manage staff in her organization, which among the following is her designation?
explanation_steps: Recruiting, training/developing and managing employees is the job of the personnel (human-resources) manager.
‘Personal’ (A) and ‘Personality’ (D) are word traps; business and administrative managers have wider duties. Answer: C.
tips: Personnel = staff/employees; personal = private.

similar_questions.stem: Which department normally handles hiring and training of workers?
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics – functions of management; Oxford Learner's Dictionary – personnel

questions.stem: How many administrative zones are there in NUEYS administrative structure?
explanation_steps: The National Union of Eritrean Youth and Students (NUEYS) is organised through branch offices in each of Eritrea's six administrative regions (zobas: Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Northern Red Sea, Southern Red Sea), which divide into sub-zones.
So its structure has 6 zones. Answer: C.
tips: Eritrea has 6 zobas; national unions (NUEYS, NUEW, NCEW) mirror them.

similar_questions.stem: How many administrative regions (zobas) does Eritrea have?
explanation_steps: Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Northern Red Sea, Southern Red Sea = 6. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – ‘The SRSR NUEYS branch …’ (branch offices in the six regions)

questions.review_flag: Assumes ‘zones’ = the six regional branches; NUEYS also has branches abroad, which some might count as a further zone.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> considered an archeological site in Eritrea at present?
explanation_steps: Qohaito (ancient town on the Akele Guzai plateau), Adulis (Aksumite port near Zula) and Buya (Danakil; 1-million-year-old hominid fossils) are well-known archaeological sites.
Asmara has archaeological sites within the city (Sembel, Mai Hutsa, pre-Aksumite settlements) and its modernist centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2017).
Tesseney is a modern market town in Gash-Barka with no recognised archaeological site. Answer: B.
tips: Eritrean archaeological sites: Adulis, Qohaito, Metera, Keskese, Belew Kelew, Buya, Sembel (Asmara).

similar_questions.stem: The ancient port of the Aksumite kingdom on the Eritrean coast was
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea National Museum / Commission of Culture and Sports; UNESCO – Asmara: A Modernist African City

questions.review_flag: Asmara (D) is mainly famous as a modern city (UNESCO for its modernist architecture), so a student might pick it; keyed B because Asmara also contains archaeological sites (Sembel, Mai Hutsa).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a land locked country?
explanation_steps: Rwanda has no coastline (neighbours: Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, DR Congo).
Eritrea (Red Sea), South Africa, Liberia and Cameroon (Atlantic/Indian Ocean) all have coasts. Answer: A.
tips: East African landlocked states: Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi.

similar_questions.stem: Which African country is landlocked?
explanation_steps: Ethiopia has had no coast since 1993. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Into how many time zones is the world divided?
explanation_steps: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so it is divided into 24 standard time zones of 15° longitude each (360 ÷ 24 = 15).
(Some countries use half-hour offsets, but the basic system has 24 zones.) Answer: C.
tips: 15° longitude = 1 hour.

similar_questions.stem: Two places are 45° of longitude apart. Their time difference is
explanation_steps: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Standard time; Time zone

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs expresses the relationship most similar to the “DOCTOR: HOSPITAL” pair?
explanation_steps: Relationship: a professional and the place where he/she WORKS.
A professor works at a college. A fan visits a stadium, a criminal is held in jail, a cow lives on a farm, food is sold in a store – none is a worker's workplace. Answer: C.
tips: State the relationship as a sentence (‘a doctor works in a hospital’) and test each option.

similar_questions.stem: TEACHER : SCHOOL is like
explanation_steps: A chef works in a kitchen. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following two months are named after Roman emperors?
explanation_steps: July is named after Julius Caesar and August after Augustus, the first Roman emperor.

(Julius Caesar was a dictator, not formally an emperor, but these are the two months named after Roman rulers.) January – Janus, March – Mars, June – Juno; September/October mean ‘seventh’/‘eighth’. Answer: D.
tips: July – Julius Caesar; August – Augustus.

similar_questions.stem: The month March is named after the Roman god of
explanation_steps: Mars, god of war. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Sara made an average of 3 trips per week for 4 weeks. How many trips does she need to make in the fifth week to raise her average to 4 trips per week?
explanation_steps: Trips so far = 3 × 4 = 12.
For an average of 4 over 5 weeks she needs 4 × 5 = 20 trips.
Week 5 = 20 − 12 = 8. Answer: C.
tips: Average problems: work with totals (average × count).

similar_questions.stem: A student averaged 60 in 3 tests. What must she score in the 4th test to average 65?
explanation_steps: Needed total 65 × 4 = 260; has 180; 260 − 180 = 80. Answer: D.

questions.stem: When typing on a computer, in order to delete the selected item, we can press one of the following keys.
explanation_steps: When text or a file is selected, pressing either Delete (Del) or Backspace removes it.
Ctrl is a modifier key and Insert toggles overwrite mode. Answer: C.
tips: Without a selection: Backspace deletes to the left of the cursor, Delete to the right.

similar_questions.stem: Which key combination copies selected text in most programs?
explanation_steps: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+Z undo. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Write down the number which will complete the sequence: 48, 24, 72, 36, 108, …
explanation_steps: Next: 108 ÷ 2 = 54. Answer: C.
tips: If differences don't work, try ratios, and look for alternating rules.

explanation_steps: Alternate ×2, −3: 11 × 2 = 22. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs expresses the relationship most similar to the “AUTHOR : BOOK” pair?
explanation_steps: Relationship: a creator and what he/she creates, in that order (author writes a book).
Composer : Song keeps the same order. Poem : Poet and Ring : Goldsmith are reversed; Carpenter : Hammer is worker : tool; Cyclist : Bicycle is user : thing used. Answer: D.
tips: Keep the ORDER of the pair as well as the relationship.

similar_questions.stem: PAINTER : PICTURE is like
explanation_steps: Creator : creation in the same order. Answer: B.

questions.stem: In a given system of coding, SISTER is coded as 535301, UNCLE as 84670 and BOY as 129. How is RUSTIC written in this code?
explanation_steps: Read letter by letter: SISTER → S=5, I=3, S=5, T=3, E=0, R=1; UNCLE → U=8, N=4, C=6, L=7, E=0; BOY → B=1, O=2, Y=9.
RUSTIC → R=1, U=8, S=5, T=3, I=3, C=6 → 185336. Answer: B.
tips: Build a letter → digit table from the examples, then code the new word.

similar_questions.stem: If CAT = 312 and TEA = 241, what is EAT?
explanation_steps: C=3, A=1, T=2, E=4 → EAT = 4 1 2. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Dead Sea is found in
explanation_steps: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Jordan, Israel and the West Bank in the Middle East (south-west Asia); its shore (about −430 m) is the lowest land on Earth.
Answer: A.
tips: Dead Sea: saltiest large lake, lowest land point.

similar_questions.stem: The lowest point in Africa is found in
explanation_steps: Lake Assal, Djibouti, about −155 m (the Danakil/Afar depression also reaches below −100 m in Eritrea). Answer: A.

questions.stem: Find the <u>odd</u> one out.
explanation_steps: Ping-pong (table tennis), rugby and bowling are all ball games; boxing is a combat sport played without a ball.
‘Ball’ (A) is also odd in a different way – it is equipment, not a sport – so A is accepted too. Keyed E; A also accepted.
tips: In odd-one-out items, check whether more than one grouping is possible.

similar_questions.stem: Find the odd one out.
explanation_steps: All but wrestling are ball games. Answer: D.

questions.review_flag: Two groupings: boxing is the only sport without a ball (E); ‘ball’ is the only item that is not a sport (A). Keyed E, A also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: Hassan likes to
explanation_steps: After ‘likes to’ we need the base form of a verb (to-infinitive): ‘to play’.
The game is called ‘catch’, and one PLAYS catch. ‘does’ and ‘did’ cannot follow ‘to’; ‘do catch’ is not idiomatic. Answer: A.
tips: to + base verb (to play, to go, to read).

similar_questions.stem: She wants ____ football after school.
explanation_steps: want + to-infinitive. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Learner's Dictionary – like (like to do); catch (the game)

questions.stem: The study of day-to-day variations in weather is called
explanation_steps: Meteorology studies the atmosphere and short-term (day-to-day) weather and forecasting.
Climatology studies long-term average weather (climate); metrology is the science of measurement; geology – rocks; hydrology – water. Answer: B.
tips: Weather (days) → meteorology; climate (30+ years) → climatology. Don't confuse metrology (measurement).

similar_questions.stem: The study of the average weather of a place over many years is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Who among the following athletes smashed three records at Daegu Marathon 2022 in South Korea?
explanation_steps: On 3 April 2022 Eritrea's Nazret Weldu won the Daegu Marathon women's race in 2:21:56.
She broke the course record (2:23:28), the Eritrean national record and her personal best (2:28:07) – three records. Answer: E.
tips: Nazret Weldu – marathon; she later improved the national record to 2:20:29 at the 2022 World Championships (4th).

similar_questions.stem: Nazret Weldu represents Eritrea mainly in which event?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: the-sports.org – Daegu Marathon 2022 results; Maeil Shinmun (3 April 2022)
textbook_ref.note: As at March 2023. She set a further national record (2:20:29) at the July 2022 World Championships.

questions.stem: The word MAN is coded as NBO. Which of the following should be the code for SKY?
explanation_steps: Each letter moves one place forward in the alphabet: M→N, A→B, N→O.
S→T, K→L, Y→Z gives TLZ. Answer: C.
tips: Write the alphabet positions and find the shift.

similar_questions.stem: If CAT is coded as DBU, then DOG is coded as
explanation_steps: Shift +1: D→E, O→P, G→H. Answer: A.

questions.stem: What is the missing letter in this series? b e h k n ? t
explanation_steps: Alphabet positions: b=2, e=5, h=8, k=11, n=14 – each is 3 more than the last.
tips: Convert letters to numbers (a=1 … z=26).

similar_questions.stem: Find the next letter: A, D, G, J, ?
explanation_steps: +3 each time: J(10) + 3 = M(13). Answer: C.

questions.stem: If you unscramble the letters YKANE, you will get the name of a
explanation_steps: Y-K-A-N-E rearranged spells KENYA, a country in East Africa.
Answer: D.
tips: Try capital first letters of common names.

similar_questions.stem: Unscramble ANIHC: it is the name of a
explanation_steps: ANIHC → CHINA. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Saleh walks 7 km to the north then turns left and walks 3 km. Then he again turns left and continues walking this time for 7 km. How many km is he away from the starting point?
explanation_steps: North 7 km; turning left from north means facing west: 3 km west.
Turning left again means facing south: 7 km south, which cancels the 7 km north.
He ends 3 km west of the start. Answer: C.
tips: Draw the path; opposite moves cancel.

similar_questions.stem: Abeba walks 4 km east, then 3 km north. How far is she from her start (straight line)?
explanation_steps: √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A baby cat is called a
explanation_steps: A young cat is a kitten. Chick – young bird/chicken; puppy – young dog; duckling – young duck.
Answer: C.
tips: Young animals: kid (goat), calf (cow), foal (horse), lamb (sheep), cub (lion).

similar_questions.stem: A young goat is called a
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.stem: In a box containing 8 marbles having equal number of black and white marbles, a black marble has been drawn in the first round. The probability of drawing a white marble in the second round is
explanation_steps: The box has 4 black and 4 white. After one black is drawn (not replaced) 7 marbles remain: 3 black and 4 white.
P(white) = 4/7. Answer: D.

questions.stem: If you were a bird, you ____ in the sky.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, which of the following plants live the <u>longest</u>?
explanation_steps: Baobabs (Adansonia digitata, found in western Eritrea/Gash-Barka) can live well over 1,000 years – some African baobabs were dated at 2,000+ years.
Wild olives and junipers are also long-lived (several hundred years or more), but baobabs are the classic longest-lived; citrus and acacias live far shorter. Answer: A.
tips: Baobab: ‘tree of life’, swollen water-storing trunk, lives for millennia.

similar_questions.stem: The baobab stores water mainly in its
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Patrut et al. (2018) Nature Plants – the demise of the largest and oldest African baobabs

questions.review_flag: Olive (Olea europaea subsp. cuspidata) and juniper trees in the highlands can also be centuries old; keyed A (baobab) as the best-known longest-lived tree.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the amount of rainfall decreases with
explanation_steps: The summer (kremti) rains come from the south-west monsoon, so rainfall is highest in the south (Debub, southern Gash-Barka) and falls towards the north (northern Anseba, Northern Red Sea, Sahel).
Rainfall generally increases, not decreases, with altitude. Answer: A.
tips: Eritrea: rain decreases northwards and towards the coastal plain (except the eastern escarpment's winter rains).

similar_questions.stem: Which part of Eritrea generally gets the most summer rainfall?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the <u>oldest</u> hominids possibly representing possible links between Homo erectus and Homo sapiens was discovered in
explanation_steps: In 1995 a hominid skull about 1 million years old (‘Madam Buya’) was found at Buya in the northern Danakil depression; it shows features between Homo erectus and Homo sapiens.
Kohayto, Adulis, Belew Kelew and Sembel are much younger (pre-Aksumite/Aksumite) sites. Answer: B.
tips: Buya – ~1 million years – Danakil.

similar_questions.stem: The Buya hominid fossils were found in which part of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Abbate et al. (1998) Nature – A one-million-year-old Homo cranium from the Danakil (Afar) depression of Eritrea

explanation_steps: Goats, pigs, cows and sheep are domesticated livestock; the warthog is a wild animal.
Answer: D.

tips: Domestic vs wild is the grouping that leaves only one out.

explanation_steps: All except the zebra are domesticated. Answer: D.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, a socioeconomic factor that hinders sustainable land management is
explanation_steps: Climate, soil fertility and pests are natural (physical/biological) factors.

The land tenure system – e.g. periodic redistribution of village land (diesa) that gave farmers little incentive to invest in terraces and trees – is a socio-economic (institutional) factor. Answer: B.
tips: Socio-economic = human/institutional (tenure, poverty, population pressure, markets).

similar_questions.stem: Which is a physical (natural) factor affecting farming?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops has equivalent nutrient content with that of fish?
explanation_steps: Fish is prized for protein and omega-3 fatty acids. Linseed (flax) is the richest crop source of omega-3 (alpha-linolenic acid) and is often promoted as the plant alternative to fish.
The legumes (faba bean, lentils, peas) are rich in protein but low in omega-3. Keyed D with low confidence (plant ALA is not fully equivalent to fish EPA/DHA).
tips: Omega-3: fish (EPA/DHA), linseed/flax, walnuts, chia (ALA).

explanation_steps: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following languages belong to Afro-Asiatic language family?
explanation_steps: Tigre is a Semitic language, and Semitic is a branch of Afro-Asiatic (like Tigrinya, Arabic, Amharic).
Nara and Kunama are Nilo-Saharan; Bantu belongs to Niger-Congo. But ‘Chadic’ (e.g. Hausa) is itself a branch of Afro-Asiatic, so C is also correct. Keyed E; C also accepted.
tips: Eritrea: Afro-Asiatic = Tigrinya, Tigre, Arabic (Semitic) + Afar, Saho, Bilen, Hidareb (Cushitic); Nilo-Saharan = Kunama, Nara.

similar_questions.stem: Which Eritrean language is Nilo-Saharan?
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Afroasiatic languages; Ethnologue – Eritrea

questions.review_flag: Two correct options: Tigre (E) and Chadic (C – a branch of Afro-Asiatic). Keyed E, C also accepted – teacher decision.
